newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end week on high note.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end week on high note.

text.p: Friday 13th proved lucky for French shares with the bourse rallying strongly after U.S. inflation and retail sales data soothed away fears of a Fed tightening on interest rates, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 15 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,080.37. That represented a gain of 3.77 percent on the week
The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,085 from 2,070.5 on Thursday's close.
Volume was a busy 5.67 billion francs.

* The U.S-induced rally gave the CAC index the impetus needed to breach resistance around 2,070. But chartists say the market could consolidate next week before aiming for the next target at 2,093-94 and then 2,100, as the psychological level.
* L'Oreal showed strong gains, closing up 3.43 percent at 1,748 francs, on turnover of 180,247.

Some brokers, looking for an explanation, pointed to the strength of Swiss management, as shown in the buoyant first-half profit at Nestle, which has a 49 percent stake in the Gesparal holding company which in turn owns 53.7 percent of L'Oreal.
But others said L'Oreal was strong before Nestle's results.
* Canal Plus recovers some ground to close up 0.36 percent at 1,103 after sell-off earlier this week following news of its merger with loss-making Dutch group Nethold.
Morgan Stanley said in a research note it rated Canal Plus "underperform," reiterated its negative opinion and recommended a sell. Its target for the stock was 735 francs.

* The French government presents the 1997 budget on September 18, seen as a vital step in gaining market confidence it can master public spending and meet Maastricht criteria for joining a single European currency in 1999.
